ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $E$ and $F$ are two movable points on the side $AD$ of the square $ABCD$, satisfying $AE=DF$. Connect $CF$ and intersect $BD$ at point $G$, connect $BE$ and intersect $AG$ at point $H$. If the side length of the square is $2$, what is the minimum value of the length of segment $DH$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Take the midpoint O of AB, and connect OH and OD,\\
since it is a square ABCD,\\
therefore AB＝AD＝CD, $\angle BAD＝\angle CDA$, $\angle ADG＝\angle CDG$,\\
in $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle DCF$,\\
\[
\left\{
\begin{array}{l}
AB=CD\\
\angle BAD=\angle CDA\\
AE=DF
\end{array}
\right.
\]\\
therefore $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle DCF$ (SAS),\\
therefore $\angle 1＝\angle 2$,\\
in $\triangle ADG$ and $\triangle CDG$,\\
\[
\left\{
\begin{array}{l}
AD=CD\\
\angle ADG=\angle CDG\\
DG=DG
\end{array}
\right.
\]\\
therefore $\triangle ADG \cong \triangle CDG$ (SAS),\\
therefore $\angle 2＝\angle 3=\angle 1$,\\
since $\angle BAH+\angle 3＝\angle BAD＝90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle 1+\angle BAH＝90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle AHB＝180^\circ−90^\circ＝90^\circ$,\\
since OH is the median of Rt$\triangle ABH$,\\
therefore OH＝AO＝$\frac{1}{2}$AB＝1,\\
in Rt$\triangle AOD$,\\
$OD=\sqrt{AO^{2}＋AD^{2}}=\sqrt{1^{2}+2^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$\\
since OH＋DH＞OD,\\
therefore when points O, D, and H are collinear, the length of DH is minimal,\\
The minimum value of DH ＝ OD−OH ＝ $\boxed{\sqrt{5}−1}$.

ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, $E$ and $F$ are two movable points on the side $AD$ of the square $ABCD$, satisfying $AE=DF$. Connect $CF$ and let it intersect $BD$ at point $G$; connect $BE$ and let it intersect $AG$ at point $H$. If the side length of the square is $2$, what is the minimum value of the length of segment $DH$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Take the midpoint $O$ of $AB$, and connect $OH$ and $OD$. Since $ABCD$ is a square, $AB=AD=CD$, $\angle BAD=\angle CDA$, and $\angle ADG=\angle CDG$. In $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle DCF$, \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} AB=CD\\ \angle BAD=\angle CDA\\ AE=DF \end{array} \right. \] therefore $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle DCF$ (SAS), so $\angle 1=\angle 2$. In $\triangle ADG$ and $\triangle CDG$, \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} AD=CD\\ \angle ADG=\angle CDG\\ DG=DG \end{array} \right. \] therefore $\triangle ADG \cong \triangle CDG$ (SAS), so $\angle 2=\angle 3=\angle 1$. Since $\angle BAH+\angle 3=\angle BAD=90^\circ$, therefore $\angle 1+\angle BAH=90^\circ$, hence $\angle AHB=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ$. Since $OH$ is the median of right triangle $\triangle ABH$, therefore $OH=AO=\frac{1}{2}AB=1$. In right triangle $\triangle AOD$, $OD=\sqrt{AO^2+AD^2}=\sqrt{1^2+2^2}=\sqrt{5}$. Since $OH+DH>OD$, when points $O$, $D$, and $H$ are collinear, the length of $DH$ is minimal. Thus the minimum value of $DH$ is $OD-OH=\boxed{\sqrt{5}-1}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; E and F are located on the upper side AD, and E is to the left of F. It is known that the side length of the square is 2, and AE=DF. Because ABCD is a square, AB=CD, and ∠BAE=∠CDF=90°. In △ABE and △DCF, AB=CD, AE=DF, and the included angle ∠BAE=∠CDF, therefore △ABE≅△DCF (SAS), so ∠ABE=∠DCF. Also because G is on BD, and BD is the angle bisector of the right angle ∠ADC at vertex D of the square, ∠ADG=∠GDC. Also AD=CD, and DG is a common side, therefore △ADG≅△CDG (SAS), so ∠DAG=∠DCG. Since G is on CF, ∠DCG=∠DCF, so ∠DAG=∠ABE. H is on AG and H is on BE, so ∠BAH=∠BAG, ∠ABH=∠ABE. Also AB⊥AD, so ∠BAH+∠DAG=90°. Combining ∠DAG=∠ABE=∠ABH, obtain ∠BAH+∠ABH=90°, therefore ∠AHB=90°. So H is always on the circle with AB as diameter. The center of this circle is the midpoint O of AB, and the radius OH=OA=AB/2=1. Because AD=2 and AO=1, in right triangle AOD, OD=sqrt(AO^2+AD^2)=sqrt(1^2+2^2)=sqrt(5). For a point H on the circle, DH≥OD-OH=sqrt(5)-1; equality is attained when O, H, D are collinear and H is on OD. Therefore the minimum value of DH is sqrt(5)-1.

method.method_draft: Synthetic geometry/locus route. First read the diagram as a square ABCD with A top-left, B bottom-left, C bottom-right, D top-right; E and F lie on AD, CF meets diagonal BD at G, and BE meets AG at H. Let O be the midpoint of AB. Use the text condition AE=DF and the square side length 2. Prove by SAS that triangle ABE is congruent to triangle DCF, so the angle made by BE with AB matches the corresponding angle made by CF with CD. Also use that BD bisects angle ADC of the square; with G on BD and CF passing through G, prove triangle ADG is congruent to triangle CDG, giving the needed equality between the angle made by AG with AD and the angle made by CF with CD. Combine these angle equalities to show angle AHB=90 degrees. Therefore H always lies on the circle with diameter AB, whose center is O and radius OA=1. Since AD=2 and AO=1, compute OD=sqrt(2^2+1^2)=sqrt(5). The shortest possible DH from fixed point D to this circle is OD-OH=sqrt(5)-1, attained when D,H,O are collinear.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $E$ and $F$ are two movable points on the side $AD$ of the square $ABCD$, satisfying $AE=DF$. Connect $CF$ and let it intersect $BD$ at point $G$; connect $BE$ and let it intersect $AG$ at point $H$. If the side length of the square is $2$, what is the minimum value of the length of segment $DH$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Take the midpoint $O$ of $AB$, and connect $OH$ and $OD$. Since $ABCD$ is a square, $AB=AD=CD$, $\angle BAD=\angle CDA$, and $\angle ADG=\angle CDG$. In $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle DCF$,
\[
\left\{
\begin{array}{l}
AB=CD\\
\angle BAD=\angle CDA\\
AE=DF
\end{array}
\right.
\]
therefore $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle DCF$ (SAS), so $\angle 1=\angle 2$. In $\triangle ADG$ and $\triangle CDG$,
\[
\left\{
\begin{array}{l}
AD=CD\\
\angle ADG=\angle CDG\\
DG=DG
\end{array}
\right.
\]
therefore $\triangle ADG \cong \triangle CDG$ (SAS), so $\angle 2=\angle 3=\angle 1$. Since $\angle BAH+\angle 3=\angle BAD=90^\circ$, therefore $\angle 1+\angle BAH=90^\circ$, hence $\angle AHB=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ$. Since $OH$ is the median of right triangle $\triangle ABH$, therefore $OH=AO=\frac{1}{2}AB=1$. In right triangle $\triangle AOD$, $OD=\sqrt{AO^2+AD^2}=\sqrt{1^2+2^2}=\sqrt{5}$. Since $OH+DH>OD$, when points $O$, $D$, and $H$ are collinear, the length of $DH$ is minimal. Thus the minimum value of $DH$ is $OD-OH=\boxed{\sqrt{5}-1}$.

The diagonal BD is connected in the figure; the line segment from C to F intersects BD at G; the line segment from A to G further intersects the line segment from B to E at H.
Reasoning: Take the midpoint O of AB. It is known that the side length of the square is 2, and AE=DF. Because ABCD is a square, AB=CD, and ∠BAE=∠CDF=90°. In △ABE and △DCF, AB=CD, AE=DF, and the included angle ∠BAE=∠CDF, therefore △ABE≅△DCF (SAS), so ∠ABE=∠DCF.
Also because G is on BD, and BD is the angle bisector of the right angle ∠ADC at vertex D of the square, ∠ADG=∠GDC. And AD=CD, DG is a common side, therefore △ADG≅△CDG (SAS), so ∠DAG=∠DCG. Since G is on CF, ∠DCG=∠DCF, thus ∠DAG=∠ABE.
H is on AG and H is on BE, so ∠BAH=∠BAG, ∠ABH=∠ABE. Also AB⊥AD, so ∠BAH+∠DAG=90°. Combining ∠DAG=∠ABE=∠ABH, obtain ∠BAH+∠ABH=90°, therefore ∠AHB=90°.
So H is always on the circle with AB as diameter. The center of this circle is the midpoint O of AB, and the radius OH=OA=AB/2=1. Because AD=2 and AO=1, in right triangle AOD, OD=sqrt(AO^2+AD^2)=sqrt(1^2+2^2)=sqrt(5). For a point H on the circle, DH≥OD-OH=sqrt(5)-1; equality is attained when the three points O, H, and D are collinear and H is on OD. Therefore the minimum value of DH is sqrt(5)-1.
